$comment: The fund's permission law. The owner armed defaultMode bypassPermissions, so the DENY list below is the WHOLE gate and the allow list is the dormant record of what this tree actually runs. Removing or weakening a DENY entry is an edit by the fund agent with the owner's word on it; adding one needs nobody's permission. Both bash and PowerShell spellings are listed because this tree is worked from both shells on Windows.
$comment-desk-tier: THIS FILE IS THE ONLY DENY LIST. A session whose cwd is a subfolder (database/, app/, platform/) loads this file only because the cockpit's launch contract passes it explicitly (--settings <this file>, --add-dir <fund root>). A subfolder may carry its own .claude/settings.json, ADDITIVE ONLY: allow rows, no deny, no defaultMode. Close any change with a probe, never with 'it takes effect next session'. Book: app/library/law/how-we-know.md#the-law-must-be-loaded.

permissions.$comment-defaultMode: THE OWNER ARMED THIS, in their own words, after the concern was put to them: their machine, their account, their Claude Code setting. It auto-approves every prompt, so what an allow list used to protect is carried by the DENY list below ALONE - MEASURED, not assumed: under bypassPermissions a command on no allow list RAN and a denied command was REFUSED. The rails: no .env or key material, no *ARMED=True*, no *acknowledge_live_trading*, no force-push or history rewrite / reset --hard / clean -f, no --no-verify or core.hooksPath, no git add -A, no staging execution/ or the retired research/ (comment-nested-repos). Branches and worktrees are allowed for the cockpit's build branches only (comment-sync-law). Probe with a deny that stands, e.g. `git add execution/x` from the root. EXACT SCOPE, red-teamed: a Read(...) pattern resolves against the WORKSPACE ROOT - a .env reached through an --add-dir elsewhere on the disk is NOT covered. A Bash(*...*) deny is a substring match on the whole command line and DOES hold everywhere. Re-run the probe after ANY edit to this file (app/library/law/how-we-guard.md#probing-the-deny-list). Cost, knowingly bought: under bypass the SDK auto-approves before canUseTool is consulted, so no permission cards, plan approval or AskUserQuestion. To go back: delete this key.

$comment-deny.comment-session-file: The rows naming a session file guard the cookie of a logged-in DATA door: one file in the home folder, outside every repo, read only by that door's adapter. No agent prints it: the Read tool (and Grep/Glob) is refused on the file wherever it is spelled, and any bash or PowerShell command line that names it is refused as a substring. Price: a command line, commit message or board note must paraphrase the name ('the owner's session file'). Scope: this stops an accidental print, not a deliberate one (a glob or a script still reaches the file). If a broker is ever connected to that account, the cookie is a TRADING credential and leaves agent reach (CLAUDE.md, Never).
$comment-deny.comment-gateway: The rows naming the Jts folder guard a broker's local gateway used as a read-only DATA door: the only lock between local code and a real order is the gateway's Read-Only API setting, stored under its install folder. So no command line may name that folder (any case), and the Edit and Write tools may not touch it: an agent never changes, moves or reinstalls the gateway or its settings. The Read tool stays open (a status probe may read, never write). Weighed and NOT added: a substring deny on order-call names - code runs from files, so such a row guards nothing on the real path, and it would refuse every grep, audit and board note that names the calls a source scan hunts. Price: a command or a commit message that spells the folder is refused whole; paraphrase it ('the gateway's install folder').
$comment-deny.comment-sync-law: force-push, history rewrites and deleting a remote branch stay BANNED, mechanically: every such spelling is denied as a SUBSTRING (so `git -C <dir> push --force`, `push origin +main` and `push origin :main` are caught, not only the plain prefix), and app/scripts/hooks/pre-push refuses a non-fast-forward or a delete of main. Branches and worktrees are allowed only as the cockpit's build branches, landed through its land queue; everyone else works on main.
$comment-deny.comment-keys: No trading credential is read by anything in this tree; the one kind of credential a door may read is a data session cookie, by its adapter alone (comment-session-file).
$comment-deny.comment-execution: no live arming of an execution layer, from any shell, by any agent: the ARMED and live-trading rows. Only the owner arms anything, and a change to these rows is the owner's own edit.
$comment-deny.comment-nested-repos: app/, database/ and platform/ are plain folders of this one repo and are staged from the root by explicit path. The execution/ and research/ rows stay as guards: neither folder ships, and `git add execution/x` is the deny-list probe that must come back REFUSED.
$comment-deny.comment-git-hooks: the commit guard (app/scripts/hooks, installed by fundd as core.hooksPath in every repo here) checks each agent commit's paths against its writes in its roster file (app/agents/<id>.md) and refuses secret material. Skipping it with --no-verify or re-pointing core.hooksPath would make it a suggestion, so both spellings are denied.

$comment-launch: Claude Code reads .claude/settings.json ONLY from the launch directory, and an agent's cwd is often a subfolder. So the cockpit (app/, fundd) boots every agent with --settings <this file> and --add-dir <fund root> (app/CLAUDE.md, the launch contract). Python is the fund venv: .venv/Scripts/python.exe from the root.
$comment-hooks: PostToolUse on Read: a cockpit agent (FUND_AGENT set) reading a .md under app/library/ or platform/lab/ (app/scripts/hooks/read-hook.mjs TRACKED) is recorded by fundd (POST /api/library/read on FUNDD_PORT: 4688 in production, 4689 in dev) so the Library room can show who pulled which book. The script exits 0 on every path, has a 2.5 s cap, and does nothing without FUND_AGENT, so the owner's own sessions are unaffected.
